stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra.
Let $0 \to K \to L \to M \to 0$ be an admissible short exact sequence
of differential graded $A$-modules. Let $s : M \to L$ and $\pi : L \to K$
be splittings such that $\Ker(\pi) = \Im(s)$.
Then we obtain a morphism
$$
\delta = \pi \circ \text{d}_L \circ s : M \to K[1]
$$
of $\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})}$ which induces the boundary maps
in the long exact sequence of cohomology associated to the displayed short exact sequence.
hypotheses: (A,d) is a dg algebra; 0→K→L→M→0 is an admissible graded-split short exact sequence of dg A-modules, with underlying graded A-linear splittings s:M→L and π:L→K satisfying ker(π)=im(s).
conclusions: The connecting morphism δ=π·d_L·s:M→K[1] is dg A-linear and induces the long-exact-cohomology boundary maps.

reason: In a graded-split admissible short exact sequence, the off-diagonal differential pi d_L s has degree one and defines a differential graded A-map into K[1]. The standard split-cochain exact-sequence computation identifies the induced cohomology morphism with the connecting map.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra.
Let $\alpha : K \to L$ be a homomorphism of differential graded
$A$-modules. There exists a factorization
$$
\xymatrix{
K \ar[r]^{\tilde \alpha} \ar@/_1pc/[rr]_\alpha &
\tilde L \ar[r]^\pi & L
}
$$
in $\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})}$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\tilde \alpha$ is an admissible monomorphism (i.e. split injective on the underlying graded $A$-modules),
\item there is a morphism $s : L \to \tilde L$
such that $\pi \circ s = \text{id}_L$ and such that
$s \circ \pi$ is homotopic to $\text{id}_{\tilde L}$.
\end{enumerate}
hypotheses: (A,d) is a dg algebra and α:K→L a morphism of dg A-modules.
conclusions: There is a factorization K→L̃→L of α with K→L̃ an admissible monomorphism, and a dg section s:L→L̃ of L̃→L such that its associated retraction is homotopic to id on L̃.

reason: Uses the standard mapping-cylinder replacement tilde L=L⊕C(1_K), whose cone summand gives a split graded injection of K and a projection to L admitting a dg section and a chain-homotopy contracting the cone summand.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra.
Let $L_1 \to L_2 \to \ldots \to L_n$
be a sequence of composable homomorphisms of
differential graded $A$-modules.
There exists a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
L_1 \ar[r] &
L_2 \ar[r] &
\ldots \ar[r] &
L_n \\
M_1 \ar[r] \ar[u] &
M_2 \ar[r] \ar[u] &
\ldots \ar[r] &
M_n \ar[u]
}
$$
in $\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})}$ such that each $M_i \to M_{i + 1}$
is an admissible monomorphism and each $M_i \to L_i$
is a homotopy equivalence.
hypotheses:
Let $(A, \text{d})$ be a differential graded algebra.
Let $L_1 \to L_2 \to \ldots \to L_n$
be a sequence of composable homomorphisms of
differential graded $A$-modules.
conclusions:
There exists a commutative diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
L_1 \ar[r] &
L_2 \ar[r] &
\ldots \ar[r] &
L_n \\
M_1 \ar[r] \ar[u] &
M_2 \ar[r] \ar[u] &
\ldots \ar[r] &
M_n \ar[u]
}
$$
in $\text{Mod}_{(A, \text{d})}$ such that each $M_i \to M_{i + 1}$
is an admissible monomorphism and each $M_i \to L_i$
is a homotopy equivalence.

reason: Inductively applies the mapping-cylinder factorization to the composite M_{n−1}→L_{n−1}→L_n. This produces a new admissible mono M_{n−1}→M_n with a homotopy-equivalence comparison M_n→L_n while retaining strict commutativity with previous replacements.

The cited homotopy rectification lemma replaces b and b' by homotopic maps so that b lands in the middle kernel K_2 and b' kills K_2. Thus the composite is strictly zero after rectification, hence null-homotopic in the original diagram.
